reuse.why: Several consumers share getExpectedScheduleAmount, but it parallels getScheduledAmount, copies getApproxNumberThreshold, and is bypassed by the new API consumer.

duplication.why: The change adds parallel amount resolution in the API adapter and shared schedules module, and duplicates the existing approximate tolerance calculation.

placement.why: Shared schedule policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the API adapter also implements that policy instead of limiting itself to field translation.

scope.why: All edits concern expected schedule amounts or their focused tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must reconcile multiple amount policies across the new helper, API adapter, existing getScheduledAmount, and budget template calculation.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts computes expectedAmount independently of getExpectedScheduleAmount; shared/schedules.ts also calculates tolerance directly instead of calling shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts reshapes amount resolution into nested ternaries, while getExpectedScheduleAmount repeats the missing/number/range dispatch already present in getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount adds an operator parameter and an isapprox branch, but scheduleModel.toExternal retains its own amount policy outside the shared helper.
